deep.reconstruction:
PROBLEM: find the minimal surface spanning a given closed contour (Plateau's problem). This is the opening page of what Hattendorff published posthumously in 1867 as Riemann's memoir 'Ueber die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung'.

(1) Area functional. The surface is written as a graph x = x(y,z) over a domain D in the (y,z)-plane. Put p = x_y, q = x_z and W = sqrt(1+p^2+q^2). The area is M = ∬_D W dy dz.

(2) First variation. Replace x by x + δx. Then
δM = ∬ (p δx_y + q δx_z)/W dy dz.

(3) Unit normal in angular coordinates. Riemann sets
-cos r = sin r cos φ / p = sin r sin φ / q = 1/W.
That is: cos r = -1/W, sin r cos φ = p/W, sin r sin φ = q/W.
So (cos r, sin r cos φ, sin r sin φ) = (-1, p, q)/W is the unit normal (x-component first). Here r is its polar angle from the x-axis and φ its azimuth in the (y,z)-plane. Then
δM = ∬ sin r (cos φ ∂δx/∂y + sin φ ∂δx/∂z) dy dz.

(4) Integration by parts. Implicitly (my addition) δx = 0 on the given contour. This gives
δM = -∬ {∂_y(sin r cos φ) + ∂_z(sin r sin φ)} δx dy dz.
Stationarity therefore requires
∂_y(p/W) + ∂_z(q/W) = 0,
which is the minimal-surface (Lagrange) equation.

(5) First exact differential. The equation in (4) is exactly the integrability condition (P_z = Q_y) for the form P dy + Q dz with P = -sin r sin φ and Q = sin r cos φ. So
dζ = -sin r sin φ dy + sin r cos φ dz
is a complete differential, defining a conjugate function ζ.

(6) Second exact differential. Trivially dx = p dy + q dz. From (3), p = sin r cos φ · W = -tan r cos φ and q = -tan r sin φ, so
dx = -tan r cos φ dy - tan r sin φ dz.

(7) Complex variables. Put η = tan(r/2) e^{iφ} and η' = tan(r/2) e^{-iφ}. This is the stereographic projection of the Gauss map. Also put ξ = y+iz, ξ' = y-iz. Substituting dy = (dξ+dξ')/2 and dz = (dξ-dξ')/(2i) gives:
- dζ = (i sin r/2)(e^{iφ} dξ' - e^{-iφ} dξ);
- dx = -(tan r/2)(e^{-iφ} dξ + e^{iφ} dξ').
With t = tan(r/2) one has sin r = 2t/(1+t^2), tan r = 2t/(1-t^2) and ηη' = t^2. Hence:
- dζ = i(η dξ' - η' dξ)/(1+ηη');
- dx = -(η dξ' + η' dξ)/(1-ηη').

PURPOSE: these two exact forms are the starting point of the next page. There Riemann derives the integrability conditions, passes to η, η' as independent variables, and obtains ∂²ξ/∂η∂η' = 0. That yields d(x+iy) = 2H(η)dη, i.e. the Weierstrass–Enneper type representation of a minimal surface parametrized by its spherical (Gauss) image, used to solve Plateau's problem for polygonal contours.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Every step was verified, including the factors 1/2 and the signs in dζ and dx.
Unstated assumption: δx vanishes on the boundary contour. Only stationarity (a necessary condition) is derived, not minimality.

Unstated assumption: the surface is a single-valued graph x(y,z) and W>0. Also not stated: the chosen normal has cos r<0, so r>π/2, tan(r/2)>1 and 1-ηη'<0. This is harmless; the formulas are singular only at r=π/2 (vertical normal), which the graph assumption excludes.
Notational remark, not an error: the letter ζ is used for the conjugate function. On the next page the roles of letters shift (e.g. x+iy appears), which can confuse readers.

results.what: Writing the divergence-free condition as exactness of -sin r sin φ dy + sin r cos φ dz (a conjugate/stream function ζ)
results.modern_name: Conjugate minimal surface / first integral of the minimal surface equation
results.usually_credited_to: Classical; appears in Riemann's posthumous memoir (1867) and in Weierstrass/Schwarz

results.what: Using η = tan(r/2) e^{iφ} (stereographic projection of the unit normal) together with ξ = y+iz to write dx and dζ as complex 1-forms
results.modern_name: Gauss map in stereographic coordinates; preliminary to the Weierstrass–Enneper representation
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous memoir 1867, written c. 1860), Weierstrass 1866, Enneper 1864

deep.surprise_reason: This page matches the opening of Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Ueber die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Göttingen 13, 1867, ed. Hattendorff), including the stereographic variable η. Riemann's priority alongside Weierstrass for the representation via the Gauss map is already recognized. It is a draft of known published work.
